events.summary:
* WHAT...Rough bar conditions expected due to very strong ebb chop.

* WHERE...In the Main Channel of the Columbia River Bar.

* WHEN...Small Craft Advisory, until 9 AM PDT this morning.
Small Craft Advisory, from 3 AM to 9 AM PDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft,
especially when operating near to, or attempting to cross, the
Columbia River Bar.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Very strong ebb current of 7.15 kt at 502
AM Tuesday. Seas 6 ft. Ebb current of 3.74 kt at 540 PM Tuesday.
Seas 3 to 4 ft. Very strong ebb current of 7.12 kt at 551 AM
Wednesday. Seas 6 to 7 ft.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...A portion of south central Texas, including the following
counties, Bexar and Comal.

* WHEN...Until 730 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Some low-water crossings may become impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 325 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
San Antonio, Helotes, Fair Oaks Ranch, Bulverde, Shavano
Park, Hollywood Park, Cross Mountain, Timberwood Park, The
Dominion, Leon Springs, Hill Country Village, Grey Forest,
Specht Store, Anhalt, Fiesta Texas and Scenic Oaks.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Bandera, TX; Medina, TX; Uvalde, TX
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWEWX

The National Weather Service in Austin/San Antonio has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Bandera County in south central Texas...
Northwestern Medina County in south central Texas...
Northeastern Uvalde County in south central Texas...

* Until 800 AM CDT.

* At 307 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain once again across the warned area. Between 2 and 5
inches of rain have already fallen over this region within the
past 6 to 9 hours. The expected rainfall rate is 1.5 to 3.5 inches
in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly once more.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms
producing flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Medina, Tarpley, Vanderpool, Hill Country State Natural Area,
Utopia, Lost Maples State Natural Area and Lakehills.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Relative humidity values will drop to around 30 percent or lower.
Given the extremely dry fuels and hot temperatures in the upper
80s and 90s, near critical fire weather conditions are expected
for parts of northwest Minnesota, particularly in forested areas.
Any fire that does develop has the potential to quickly spread.

For more information on burning restrictions for Minnesota, see
www.dnr.state.mn.us/forestry/fire/firerating_restrictions.html
